title: AI ‘deepfakes’ give US political attack ads a new twist
source_used: Fox News Digital and HuffPost (FT headline only)
key_facts: FT headline: 'Cheap AI deepfakes give new twist to US political attack ads' (9 Oct 2026); text not readable.
AI lowers the cost of political ads; campaigns can produce in minutes or hours what took days (Fox News Digital, 5 Oct 2026).
AdImpact had identified 29 campaign ads in federal and gubernatorial races that disclosed AI content as of two weeks before 5 Oct 2026.
Wesleyan Media Project, which also counts ads without disclosure, identified at least 164 AI-influenced ads this cycle.
Consultants say it is unclear AI helps win elections.
HuffPost (via AOL): an ad by Republican Rep. Brad Finstad appeared to use an AI-generated image replacing a small business owner with Gov. Tim Walz in a photo with Democrat Jake Johnson.
quote_evidence: Artificial intelligence is dramatically lowering the cost of political advertising, allowing campaigns to churn out attack ads, memes and other targeted messages at a pace that would have been prohibitively expensive just a few years ago.
But the jury is still out on whether the use of AI for campaign messaging can help produce the ultimate objective: an election victory.
why_it_matters_hint: AI is making fake-looking political ads cheap, ahead of the midterms.
notes: Desk-built entry: FT page is paywalled (HTTP 403), so only its headline is known and it is credited as such. Facts read at Fox News Digital (5 Oct 2026) and HuffPost via AOL (Finstad ad; HuffPost says the image 'appeared to be AI-generated'). Neither is a copy of the FT. Not an exact match for the FT's specific examples.
